From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95/p99 spike + 5xxs — BlueHarbor (urgent)

I'm on it — summary of findings from initial triage (08:30–08:40 window):

What happened:
- Queue/backpressure: a subset of GPU workers serving hosted-api.prod-us.highpriority experienced slow downstream kernel handshakes for the "opt-6b-unified" model variant. Worker-side continuous batching logic accumulated more requests per batch (avg batch_size climbed from 8 -> 22), which increased tail latency for in-flight requests.
- Autoscaling lagged: replicas scaled up but with ~45s provisioning lag; during scaling batches continued to grow and queue depth rose (observed peak queue_depth ~1187).
- Result: p95/p99 regressions and an uptick in transient grpc 504s as in-flight batches exceeded soft timeouts.

Immediate mitigations pushed (08:41–08:48):
- Reduced max_batch_size for hosted-api.prod-us.highpriority from 32 -> 12 (control plane change) — effect visible within 90s.
- Increased per-route concurrency cap and enabled emergency route-burst to larger instance pool (dedicated spare pool) to absorb inflight backlog.
- Temporarily raised batch timeout from 1.2s -> 1.8s to avoid erroneous grpc timeouts while workers drained backlog.

Status now (08:50):
- queue_depth: 1187 -> 210
- p95: ~1.4s -> 420ms
- 5xx rate: 1.2% -> 0.15%

Next steps (recommended):
1) Keep reduced max_batch_size for 30–60 minutes while monitoring tail latencies.
2) Investigate root cause of kernel handshake slowdown on the specific "opt-6b-unified" worker builds (hedge: revert recent kernel micro-optimization from deployment at 07:50 that correlates with onset).
3) Add a short-term policy to avoid batch_size runaway when queue_depth > 400 (throttling at frontend).

I'll continue looking at kernel logs and queue histograms. If leadership wants to notify execs / offer credits, I'll include the impact numbers (we saw ~14k affected requests during the spike window).

—Ethan
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec summary: BlueHarbor hosted API spike resolved — immediate mitigations + follow-ups

Hi all,

Summary (incident window: 2027-05-20 08:35 – 08:55 UTC):
- Customer: BlueHarbor (high-priority hosted route)
- Impact: p95 regressed from 210ms -> 1.4s, p99 >3s; ~14k requests affected, 5xx peaked at ~1.2%
- Cause: batching/backpressure amplification due to kernel handshake slowdown on "opt-6b-unified" workers + autoscaling provisioning lag -> batch_size runaway and queue depth growth.
- Immediate mitigations performed: reduced max_batch_size, increased concurrency and route-burst to spare pool, raised batch timeout to reduce false 504s. These actions brought p95 down to ~420ms and error rate to baseline.

Actions for follow-up (owners & ETA):
- Engineering (Ethan) — Investigate kernel regression, revert micro-optimization if confirmed. ETA: 24–48h.
- Platform (Jonas) — Add frontend throttling policy when queue_depth > 400 and add route-level circuit breaker to prevent batch runaway. ETA: 72h for policy + 7d for tests.
- Customer Success (Marissa) — Coordinate a post-incident update to BlueHarbor and offer goodwill credit for the window. ETA: 48h to finalize messaging and credit amount.

Decision requested: please confirm approval to issue an expedited goodwill credit (recommendation: one week of usage credit for BlueHarbor's hosted API) and to prioritize the batch-runaway circuit breaker in next sprint.

Thanks — will keep this thread updated with root cause details and kernel analysis.

—Tessa
